claim.quote: we performed the first search for 0νββ decay in a low background condition using a detector on the scale of hundreds of kg of non-enriched Ca

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published Phys. Rev. D 103, 092008 (2021).

key_value_text.quote: The expected background rate was in a good agreement with the measured rate
key_value_text.value: background rate ~1e-3 events/keV/yr/(kg of natCa) in the 0vbb window (130.4 live days)

name: Low background measurement in CANDLES-III for studying the neutrino-less double beta decay of 48Ca

summary.plain: CANDLES III showed that a detector holding hundreds of kilograms of calcium fluoride can reach a very low background, about one event per thousand per keV per year per kilogram of calcium. It made the first low-background search for calcium-48 decay at that scale, with unenriched calcium.
summary.technical: 130.4 live days in the Kamioka underground: measured background ~1e-3 events/keV/yr/(kg of natCa) in the 0vbb window, in good agreement with Monte Carlo of crystal impurities and (n,gamma) gamma rays; first low-background 0vbb search with a detector of hundreds of kg of non-enriched Ca. No half-life limit is stated in the abstract.

title: Low background measurement in CANDLES-III for studying the neutrino-less double beta decay of 48Ca
why_it_matters: Demonstrates the background level needed before 48Ca-enriched crystals are deployed for a more sensitive search.
